title: A Picnic Shop with a Fixed Budget

questions.explanation: 原预算是 twenty-four pounds；十五是折后花费。

instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
Mina and her brother Ravi are shopping for a small neighborhood picnic. They have a budget of twenty-four pounds for food and drinks. Before leaving home, they write a list with a pound sign beside each price and agree that Ravi will check the prices while Mina carries a basket. They want enough food for six people, but they do not want to buy a large quantity that will go to waste.

At the first shelf, Mina finds a packet of beans for three pounds. They choose two packets, so the cost is six pounds. Nearby, a bag of rice has a price of four pounds. The label says that the bag contains one kilogram. Ravi also picks up carrots. A sign asks customers to weigh loose vegetables, and the scale shows a weight of one kilogram. The carrots cost four pounds.

The last item is one liter of oil for three pounds. Ravi checks the numbers on the list: six pounds for beans, four for rice, four for carrots and three for oil. The total before any reduction is seventeen pounds. Mina sees a package of paper plates, but it is expensive. There are plates at home, so they decide not to include that purchase. A cheap bag is not useful if they do not need it.

At the checkout, the assistant notices that the shop has agreed to discount their food by two pounds for a local event. The amount they need to pay is therefore fifteen pounds. Ravi plans to pay in cash with a twenty-pound note. The assistant gives him five one-pound coins as change and hands him a receipt. Mina counts every coin and checks the receipt before they leave.

Outside, the two discuss how much of the original budget remains. They spend fifteen pounds at the shop, leaving nine pounds for anything else the group decides to buy. They agree to save that money for now instead of choosing an unnecessary extra item. If the group later wants fruit, they can decide together what they can afford.

Ravi notices a poster for a similar picnic in the United States. Its example price is shown in dollars, and one small drink has a price of one dollar. The poster is not a currency exchange guide, so Mina does not compare it directly with a pound. They join a short queue to collect the picnic notice and walk home. Mina is pleased that the list and receipt explain their choices clearly.
